source_refs.note: Exercise 1.3, Question 1 (book p. 23-24); answers book p. 298-299 (PDF 300-301)

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Let \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\). Show that \(f(x)\) is a one-to-one function using the horizontal line test.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh graph wala sawal hai: humein dikhana hai ke function one-to-one (har output sirf ek input se aaye) hai, aur woh bhi horizontal line test se.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\).
Find kya karna hai? Saabit karna hai ke koi bhi horizontal line graph ko ek se zyada dafa nahin kaatti.
Plan: pehle domain, phir table bana kar graph, aur aakhir mein general line y = c le kar dikhana ke x ki sirf ek value milti hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\).
Saabit karna: f one-to-one hai, horizontal line test se.
Tareeqa: function one-to-one hota hai agar har horizontal line us ke graph ko zyada se zyada ek dafa kaate. Hum graph banayenge, phir f(x) = c ko general c ke liye solve kar ke dikhayenge ke x ek hi aata hai. Sirf graph dekh kar kehna kaafi nahin, isi liye algebra se bhi pakka karenge.

Domain nikalein
\[x - 2 > 0\]
\[x > 2\]
Kyun: logarithm sirf positive numbers ka hota hai. Zero ya negative ka log exist nahin karta, is liye bracket ke andar wali cheez zero se bari honi chahiye.
Dhyan dein: \(x = 2\) bhi allowed nahin, kyun ke \(\log_{4}0\) defined nahin.

Values ki table banayein
\[x = 2.25:\ \log_{4}\tfrac{1}{4} = -1\]
\[x = 3:\ \log_{4}1 = 0\]
\[x = 6:\ \log_{4}4 = 1\]
\[x = 18:\ \log_{4}16 = 2\]
Kyun: hum \(x\) aise chunte hain ke \(x - 2\) 4 ki koi power ho (\(\frac{1}{4}, 1, 4, 16\)). Is tarah log ki value seedha poora number aa jati hai aur calculator ki zaroorat nahin padti.

Graph ki shakal
\(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\) asal mein \(y = \log_{4}x\) ka graph hai jo 2 units daayen sarak gaya. Is liye vertical asymptote \(x = 0\) se \(x = 2\) par aa gaya, aur \(x\)-axis ko \((1, 0)\) ki jagah \((3, 0)\) par kaatta hai. Base \(4 > 1\) hai, is liye graph hamesha oopar chadhta (strictly increasing) hai.
Kyun: yeh \(f(x - h)\) ki shakal hai jahan \(h = 2\); Section 1.9 ke mutabiq \(h > 0\) ka matlab daayen shift.

\(y = c\) se horizontal line test
\[\log_{4}(x - 2) = c\]
\[x - 2 = 4^{c}\]
\[x = 4^{c} + 2\]
Kyun: \(\log_{a}u = c\) ka matlab hai \(u = a^{c}\) (log ko exponential form mein badla). Ab \(c\) jo bhi ho, \(4^{c}\) ki sirf ek value hai, is liye \(x\) bhi sirf ek. Aur \(4^{c}\) hamesha positive hai, is liye \(x = 4^{c} + 2 > 2\), yani yeh \(x\) domain ke andar hai.
Dhyan dein: sirf ek line (masalan \(y = 1\)) check karna saboot nahin; general \(c\) lena zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq:
Line \(y = 1\) graph ko sirf \((6, 1)\) par milti hai aur \(y = 2\) sirf \((18, 2)\) par. Figure mein har dashed line curve ko ek hi dafa kaat rahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Har horizontal line \(y = c\) graph ko bilkul ek dafa kaatti hai (\(x = 4^{c} + 2\) par). Saabit ho gaya: \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\) one-to-one hai.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = log base 4 of (x - 2) rising from the dashed asymptote x = 2 through (2.25, -1), (3, 0), (6, 1) and (18, 2); the dashed horizontal lines y = -1, y = 1 and y = 2 each cut the curve exactly once.
answer_figure.caption: f(x) = log₄(x − 2) with horizontal lines: each meets the curve once

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Let \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\). Find the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) algebraically.
blocks.explanation:
Ab inverse function algebra se nikalna hai, graph se nahin.
Diya kya hai? \(y = \log_{4}(x - 2)\), aur part (i) se pata hai ke yeh one-to-one hai, is liye inverse maujood hai.
Find kya karna hai? \(f^{-1}(x)\) ka formula.
Plan: log form ko exponential form mein badlein, \(x\) ko akela karein, phir \(x\) aur \(y\) ki jagah badal dein.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\), jo one-to-one hai (part (i)).
Maloom karna: \(f^{-1}(x)\).
Tareeqa: \(y = f(x)\) likh kar \(x\) ko \(y\) ki shakal mein nikalein, phir \(x\) aur \(y\) interchange karein. Inverse woh function hai jo \(f\) ka kaam ulta kar de, is liye hum \(f\) ke rule ko peeche ki taraf chalate hain.

\(y = f(x)\) likhein
\[y = \log_{4}(x - 2)\]
Kyun: inverse isi rule ko ulta karega, is liye shuruaat yahin se.

Exponential form mein badlein
\[4^{y} = x - 2\]
Kyun: \(\log_{a}u = y\) aur \(a^{y} = u\) ek hi baat ke do roop hain. Log ko hatane ka yahi seedha raasta hai: base 4 ko \(y\) ki power di aur bracket wali cheez doosri taraf aa gayi.

\(x\) ko akela karein
\[x = 4^{y} + 2\]
Kyun: dono taraf 2 jama kiya taa ke x akela reh jaye.

\(x\) aur \(y\) interchange karein
\[y = 4^{x} + 2\]
\[f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\]
Kyun: inverse function \(f\) ke outputs ko input ke taur par leta hai, is liye \(x\) aur \(y\) ka kirdar badal jata hai. Hum aam taur par input ko \(x\) hi kehte hain, isi liye aakhir mein naam badle.
Dhyan dein: \(4^{x} + 2\) ko \(4^{x + 2}\) mat likhiye; 2 power mein nahin, bahar jama ho raha hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[f(f^{-1}(x)) = \log_{4}(4^{x} + 2 - 2)\]
\[= \log_{4}4^{x} = x\]
\(f\) ko jawab par lagaya to \(x\) wapas mil gaya; yani dono ek doosre ka kaam ulta karte hain.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Let \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\). State the domain and range of \(f(x)\) and \(f^{-1}(x)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh domain aur range likhne ka sawal hai, do functions ke liye.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\) aur part (ii) se \(f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\).
Find kya karna hai? Chaaron cheezein: f ka domain aur range, inverse ka domain aur range.
Rule: inverse inputs aur outputs ki jagah badal deta hai, is liye f ka domain inverse ki range banta hai aur f ki range inverse ka domain.
Plan: pehle f ke liye nikalein, phir swap karein, phir inverse ke formula se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\), \(f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\).
Maloom karna: \(D_{f}, R_{f}, D_{f^{-1}}, R_{f^{-1}}\).
Tareeqa: inverse mein input aur output ki jagah badal jati hai, is liye ek ka domain doosre ki range hoti hai. Sirf f ke liye mehnat karni hai, baqi swap se mil jayega.

\(f\) ka domain
\[x - 2 > 0 \Rightarrow x > 2\]
\[D_{f} = \,]2, \infty[\]
Kyun: log ke andar positive number chahiye. Bracket ulte \(]\ [\) is liye ke 2 shamil nahin (open interval).

\(f\) ki range
\[R_{f} = \,]-\infty, \infty[\]
Kyun: jab \(x\) \(]2, \infty[\) mein chalta hai to \(x - 2\) har positive value leta hai, aur log har positive number par har real value deta hai. Part (i) mein bhi dekha ke har line \(y = c\) graph ko milti hai, yani har \(c\) output hai.

\(f^{-1}\) ka domain aur range
\[D_{f^{-1}} = R_{f} = \,]-\infty, \infty[\]
\[R_{f^{-1}} = D_{f} = \,]2, \infty[\]
Kyun: input aur output ki adla badli; jo f ke liye input tha woh inverse ke liye output hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(4^{x}\) har real \(x\) ke liye defined hai, is liye domain poori real line. Aur \(4^{x} > 0\) hamesha, is liye \(4^{x} + 2 > 2\), aur yeh 2 se oopar har value leta hai. Bilkul wahi jo swap se aaya.
Dhyan dein: range mein 2 shamil nahin, kyun ke \(4^{x}\) kabhi zero nahin hota.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Let \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\). Verify graphically that the graphs of \(f(x)\) and \(f^{-1}(x)\) are symmetric about the line \(y = x\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh graph se tasdeeq ka sawal hai: dono graphs aur line y = x ek hi plane par banane hain.
Diya kya hai? \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\) aur \(f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\).
Find kya karna hai? Dikhana ke dono graphs y = x ke aar paar aaine ki tarah (symmetric) hain.
Plan: f ke points lein, un ke coordinates ulat kar inverse ke points banayein, aur saabit karein ke har jora y = x mein ek doosre ka aks hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\), \(f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\).
Tasdeeq karna: dono graphs \(y = x\) ke gird symmetric hain.
Tareeqa: \((a, b)\) graph \(f\) par ho to \((b, a)\) graph \(f^{-1}\) par hota hai, aur \((b, a)\) asal mein \((a, b)\) ka \(y = x\) mein reflection hai. To agar har point ka aks doosre graph par ho, poora graph aks hai.

f ke points aur inverse ke points
\[(2.25, -1) \leftrightarrow (-1, 2.25)\]
\[(3, 0) \leftrightarrow (0, 3)\]
\[(6, 1) \leftrightarrow (1, 6)\]
Ek check: \(4^{1} + 2 = 6\), to \((1, 6)\) waqai \(f^{-1}\) par hai.
Kyun: inverse ka har point f ka point hi hai, bas coordinates ki jagah badli hui. Yeh points part (i) ki table se liye.

\((b, a)\), \((a, b)\) ka aks kyun hai
\[\text{slope} = \dfrac{a - b}{b - a} = -1\]
\[\text{midpoint} = \left(\tfrac{a+b}{2}, \tfrac{a+b}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: dono points ko milane wali line ka slope \(-1\) hai aur \(y = x\) ka slope 1; in ka product \(-1\) hai, yani dono perpendicular (90 degree par) hain. Midpoint ke dono coordinates barabar hain, yani midpoint \(y = x\) par hai. Aaina bilkul beech mein aur seedha khara hai: yahi reflection ki shart hai.

Asymptotes aur intercepts bhi ulatte hain
\(f\) ka vertical asymptote \(x = 2\) inverse ka horizontal asymptote \(y = 2\) ban jata hai; \(f\) ka \(x\)-intercept \((3, 0)\) inverse ka \(y\)-intercept \((0, 3)\) ban jata hai.
Kyun: yeh sab bhi points se bane hain, aur har point ulatta hai. Graph banate waqt yeh check bohat kaam aata hai.
Dhyan dein: dono graphs ke x aur y axes par scale barabar rakhiye, warna symmetry nazar nahin aayegi.

Tasdeeq:
Figure mein dashed lines y = x par 90 degree se kat kar beech se aadhi hoti hain. Agar kaghaz ko y = x par moran to ek curve bilkul doosre par aa girega.
blocks.final_answer: \(f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\) ka graph \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\) ke graph ka line \(y = x\) mein reflection hai, is liye dono graphs \(y = x\) ke gird symmetric hain.

answer_figure.alt: The curve f(x) = log base 4 of (x - 2) with asymptote x = 2, the curve f inverse (x) = 4 to the power x plus 2 with asymptote y = 2, and the line y = x. Dashed segments join (3, 0) to (0, 3), (6, 1) to (1, 6) and (2.25, -1) to (-1, 2.25), each cut in half by y = x.
answer_figure.caption: f and f⁻¹ are mirror images in the line y = x

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein Question 1 ke liye label (iii) do dafa chhapa hai. Doosra (iii), jis mein \(f(x) = \log_{4}(x - 2)\) aur \(f^{-1}(x) = 4^{x} + 2\) ke graphs hain, asal mein part (iv) ka jawab hai.
